lectures.title: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha

items: **Constitutional Basis:** governed under **Part V (Articles 93–96, 100, 110, 118)**; chosen/elected by the Lok Sabha from among its sitting members (**Art. 93**).
**Membership Requirement:** must already be an elected MP of Lok Sabha at the time of election; a non-member cannot be chosen as Speaker under the 6-month relaxation rule.
**Election date:** the **President** fixes the date of election of the Speaker.
**Oath of Office:** the Speaker takes **NO separate oath of office** as presiding officer; takes oath solely as an ordinary Member of Parliament.
**Administrative Control:** the **Lok Sabha Secretariat** functions directly under the control and guidance of the Speaker.
**Resignation Route (Art. 94(b)):** the Speaker addresses the resignation in writing to the **Deputy Speaker** (reciprocal: the Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker).
**Trap:** the resignation goes across laterally, **NOT upward to the President**.

**Effect of Dissolution (Universal Exception Trap):** when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Speaker does NOT vacate office immediately; continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.
**Removal Mechanism (Art. 94(c)):** removed only by a resolution passed by a majority of **ALL THE THEN MEMBERS** of the Lok Sabha (**Effective Majority**).
**Notice for removal:** requires at least **14 days'** advance written notice before moving the resolution.

parts.t: Special constitutional powers and functions of the Speaker
items: **Money Bill Certification (Art. 110(4)):** sole and final authority to certify whether a Bill is a Money Bill; the endorsement is final when transmitted to Rajya Sabha and presented to the President.
**Presiding over Joint Sittings (Art. 118(4)):** presides over joint sittings of both Houses of Parliament; in absence: Deputy Speaker, then Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
**Maintenance of Order:** adjourns the House or suspends sittings in the absence of a **Quorum** (1/10th strength under Art. 100); exercises **Adjournment Sine Die**.
**Anti-Defection Disqualifications:** decides questions of member disqualification arising out of defection under the **10th Schedule** (subject to judicial review per **Kihoto Hollohan**).
**Fixing Deputy Speaker Election:** the Speaker fixes the date for the election of the Deputy Speaker under **Rule 8(1)**.

parts.t: Deputy Speaker: framework, election and convention
items: **Constitutional Framework:** governed under **Part V (Articles 93–96)**; chosen/elected by the Lok Sabha from among its sitting members (**Art. 93**).
**Election Date Authority (Rule 8(1)):** the date of election of the Deputy Speaker is fixed by the **Speaker of Lok Sabha** (communicated to all members by the Secretary-General).
**Constitutional Status vs Convention:** the Constitution does NOT mandate that the Deputy Speaker must belong to the Opposition.
**Convention:** selection of the Deputy Speaker from the Opposition is a parliamentary convention/practice, NOT a mandatory constitutional requirement.
**Oath of Office:** like the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker takes NO separate oath of office as presiding officer (takes oath solely as an ordinary MP).

parts.t: Deputy Speaker: powers and privileges while presiding (Art. 95)
items: **Equality of Powers:** when presiding over a sitting of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Speaker exercises the same powers as the Speaker.
**Finality of Rulings:** there is no appeal to the Speaker against any ruling given by the Deputy Speaker while in the Chair.
**Joint Sittings (Art. 118(4)):** presides over Joint Sittings of Parliament if the Speaker is absent.
**Parliamentary Committees:** if appointed to any Parliamentary Committee, the Deputy Speaker automatically becomes its **Chairman**.

parts.t: Deputy Speaker: floor rights and important traps
items: Floor rights: normal sittings vs own removal (Art. 96)
**During Normal Proceedings (when NOT in the Chair):** sits as an ordinary member of the House; can participate in debates, move motions, and vote in the first instance.
**During Consideration of Own Removal Resolution (Art. 96):** cannot preside over the sitting even if present in the House.
**Speak and vote:** during own removal resolution, has the right to speak, participate, and vote in the first instance.
**Casting vote:** during own removal resolution, cannot exercise a casting vote in case of an equality of votes (tie).
**Lateral Resignation Trap:** the Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker, NOT to the President or Prime Minister.
**Dissolution Protection Distinction:** the special constitutional protection to continue holding office after the dissolution of Lok Sabha applies only to the **Speaker**, NOT the Deputy Speaker.
**Removal Majority:** requires a majority of all the then members of Lok Sabha (**Effective Majority**), NOT a Simple Majority or 2/3rd Special Majority.

lectures.title: Sessions of Parliament and minimum ages of members

items: **Constitutional Framework:** governed under **Part V (Article 85)**; the President summons each House of Parliament at such time and place as they think fit.
**Six-Month Rule:** the maximum gap between two consecutive sessions cannot exceed **6 months**.
**Wording of the rule:** six months shall not intervene between the last sitting in one session and the date appointed for the first sitting in the next session.
**Mandate:** the Constitution mandates that Parliament must meet **at least twice a year**.
**Number of sessions:** the Constitution does NOT specify a fixed number of sessions; having 3 sessions (**Budget, Monsoon, Winter**) is a parliamentary convention.
**Sitting days:** the Constitution does NOT prescribe a minimum number of sitting days in a year.

**Prorogation & Advice:** the President exercises prorogation on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, not at absolute personal discretion.
**Maximum interval** between two Parliamentary sessions = **6 Months** (Art. 85).
**Maximum validity of an Ordinance** after reassembly = **6 Weeks** (Art. 123).
**Maximum possible lifespan of an Ordinance** without approval = **6 Months + 6 Weeks**.
**60 days:** an MP's unexcused absence of 60 days can lead to vacation of the seat.
**Exclusion Rule:** the calculation strictly excludes periods of Prorogation and Adjournments exceeding 4 consecutive days.
**Fixed Calendar Fallacy:** any option claiming "The Constitution mandates three sessions: Budget, Monsoon, and Winter" is FALSE (only the 6-month maximum gap is constitutionally mandated).
**Minimum Days Trap:** any option stating "Parliament must sit for a minimum of 60/90/100 days per year" is FALSE (no minimum days prescribed in the Constitution).

parts.t: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund
items: **Charged Expenditure (Non-Votable):** can be discussed by both Houses of Parliament, but is NOT submitted to the vote of Parliament.
**Charged vs. Voted Rule (Arts. 112 & 202):** charged expenditure can be discussed in Parliament/State Legislature, but is NOT submitted to vote.
**Purpose:** guaranteed by the Constitution to maintain the financial independence of constitutional offices.
Expenditures specifically charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 112(3))
**President:** emoluments and allowances of the President and office expenses.
**Presiding officers:** salaries, allowances, and pensions of the Chairman & Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, and Speaker & Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha.
**Supreme Court:** salaries, allowances, and pensions of Judges of the Supreme Court.
**High Court Judges:** pensions ONLY of High Court Judges (Classic Trap).
**CAG:** salary, allowances, and pensions of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).
**Debt charges** for which the Government of India is liable (interest, sinking fund charges).
**Judgments:** any sum required to satisfy any judgment, decree, or arbitral award against the Government of India.

parts.t: Salaries of the presiding officers of Parliament
Who is NOT charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
items: **Vice-President's Salary:** the Vice-President receives NO salary as Vice-President; salary is drawn in the capacity of Chairman of Rajya Sabha (which is charged).
**Prime Minister & Union Ministers:** salaries and allowances of the Prime Minister and other Ministers are **VOTABLE** (NOT charged).
**Election Commission of India (ECI):** salaries and administrative expenses of CEC and Election Commissioners are NOT charged on the CFI (Source PYQ distinction).

**High Court Judges (The Dual-Fund Trap):** Salaries & Allowances: charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State (Art. 202(3)); Pensions: charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 112(3)(d)(iii)).
**Governor's Emoluments:** charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

**Constitutional Insertion:** introduced via the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985** (added the **10th Schedule**; amended Articles 101, 102, 190, and 191).
**Key Dates:** the Anti-Defection Bill received the President's assent on **15 February 1985**; came into force on **1 March 1985**.
**First Constitutional Recognition:** political parties were explicitly recognized in the Constitution for the first time through this amendment.
**Pre-1985 Regional Precedent:** **Jammu & Kashmir** enacted its own state Anti-Defection legislation earlier in **1979**.
**Subsequent Tightening:** strengthened by the **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** (deleted the 1/3rd "split" exception and capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lower House).
**Disqualification trigger:** voluntarily gives up party membership (broader than formal resignation; includes conduct).
**Disqualification trigger:** votes or abstains contrary to the party whip without prior permission.
**Safe harbor:** prior permission obtained, or action condoned by the party within **15 days**.
**Merger:** ≥ 2/3rd of the legislature party agrees to merge with another party.

parts.t: Who decides: defection versus general disqualification
items: Presiding Officer (Speaker / Chairman of the concerned House)
Acts as a tribunal; NO consultation with ECI; subject to Judicial Review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992)
Mandatory & binding opinion of the Election Commission of India (ECI)
**Deciding Head Trap:** the President or Governor has NO jurisdiction over 10th Schedule defection matters; it is decided solely by the Speaker/Chairman.
**Time-Frame Myth:** the 10th Schedule prescribes NO statutory time limit within which the Presiding Officer must decide a defection petition.

**Current Law (merger):** disqualification does not apply if a member's original political party merges with another party and not less than **two-thirds (2/3rd)** of the legislature party members agree to the merger.
**Trap:** defection protection for a 1/3rd "split" has been completely abolished.
**Nominated Member Window:** nominated members have a 6-month window to join a party; after 6 months, joining any party triggers disqualification.

**"Voluntarily Giving Up Membership":** an MP/MLA's conduct (e.g., publicly campaigning for an opposition party) can constitute voluntarily giving up membership even without submitting a formal letter of resignation.
